hints: Look carefully at the four curves from 00:00 to 24:00. Which curve stays below all the others for almost the whole day, especially around midday?
Remember what a xerophyte is adapted for. In the same hot, dry midday conditions, should it lose more water or much less water than a normal plant?
walkthrough:
**Observe the graph**

Look at transpiration rate on the y-axis against time of day on the x-axis. All four plants start low at 00:00, rise to a peak around midday, then fall again.

The key difference is height. One curve is clearly the lowest at every time point.

**Recall xerophyte adaptations**

A xerophyte lives in dry conditions and must conserve water. Think thick cuticle, sunken stomata, reduced leaves and stomatal closure at midday.

All of these adaptations act to reduce water loss, so:
$$xerophyte = lowest\ transpiration\ rate$$

**Pick the lowest curve**

Curve D stays well below A, B and C throughout the 24 hours, with the lowest midday peak. That is exactly what we expect for a water-conserving xerophyte.

options.A: Shows the highest transpiration rate, especially in the afternoon. This is the opposite of a water-conserving xerophyte.
options.B: Shows the second highest transpiration rate. It loses too much water to be the xerophyte.
options.C: Lower than A and B but still clearly higher than D, so it is not the best adapted to conserve water.
options.D: Shows the lowest transpiration rate at all times. This fits xerophytic adaptations that minimise water loss.
